correctness.rationale: Every nonclique face has a unique center: any two common neighbors of a nonadjacent pair would generate a four-cycle. The dimension-ordered center pairing is free at each step and partitions all nonclique faces, leaving the clique complex. The action preserves each stage. Triangle faces have disjoint edge supports and collapse to a graph; their signed boundaries form a primitive sublattice of the integral graph cycle lattice, yielding the claimed exact module and free homology. A deterministic exhaustive program checked all 8,597 C4-free labeled graphs with at most six vertices, including every individual collapse, and separately confirmed group invariance for three examples. The universal assertion rests on the proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Uniform structural result for all finite graphs without four-cycles, with exact automorphism-equivariant elementary collapse, sharp obstruction, integral triangle-boundary quotient, and explicit circle-rank formula. This upgrades the primary literature’s general fundamental-group connection to a simple-homotopy classification and natural integral symmetry representation; it is not an arbitrary small-case calculation. Its canonical radius-one graph-Cech interpretation provides a usable graph-recovery regime.
